speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At Chipping Norton. The inn's dog has taken my stool, and I have let him, which tells you how the back does.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I walked a hundred miles to Stratford with nothing worse than a raw heel, and raised one barn frame for a man's cousin, and was undone by it. This deserves to be remembered, though not repeated to Kemp.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is not much. It complains when I rise and is content when I sit, which gives it the advantage of most creditors.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Hobbins put me up on the spare nag as far as Shipston, on condition I carried nothing. I said I'd carry nothing but a thought. He said thoughts weigh nothing on a horse. He has never carried mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tomorrow the paper goes nearer the top of the wallet. No. The things I need go nearer the top, and I'll own that paper is not always among them.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There was a sentence on the road this morning. I thought I should keep it. …I remember instead that the left strap wants shortening.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Very well. The strap is useful.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am too old to walk to Warwickshire. …Three years. What's a house worth? Forty pound? A hundred? I don't know. I know what a play is worth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Mark this, though. The friar. He should come on with a basket, at first light, gathering. And in the one basket the herb that heals and the herb that kills, and he knows which is which, and says so. A man who knows that much ought to be careful. He won't be.
